message.content:
{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study compares functional connectivity changes in thalamic pain between human patients and a macaque model, reporting quantitative measures of cross-species convergence. It directly assesses how animal model findings (FC changes in macaques) align with human clinical observations.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "This study aimed to investigate functional connectivity (FC) in human patients and a macaque model of thalamic pain... Therefore, the present results suggest that the FC changes in the regions associated with emotion, memory, motivation, and reward are part of the underlying mechanisms of thalamic pain onset present in both human patients and model macaques.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "neurology-stroke",
    "pain"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Thalamic pain can be understood as a network reorganization disorder... Thalamic pain accounts for over half of all CPSP cases.",
  "model_type": "induced",
  "model_evidence": "In macaque analyses, we compared FCs before and after the injection of collagenase to induce thalamic pain.",
  "species": [
    "non-human-primate"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "In humans, resting-state FC was compared between patients with thalamic pain and healthy individuals. Furthermore, resting-state FC was compared in macaques, before and after the induction of thalamic pain in the same individuals.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "This study aimed to investigate functional connectivity (FC) in human patients and a macaque model of thalamic pain... FC between the amygdala of the unaffected hemisphere and the brainstem was significantly higher in patients with thalamic pain."
}
